inspection_summary: Inspected all 669 normalized lines. The usable mathematical arc runs from the Pólya equivalence between RH and Jensen-polynomial hyperbolicity, through a general Hermite scaling limit for locally quadratic logarithmic sequence growth, to an all-orders saddle-point analysis of central completed-zeta derivatives and both asymptotic and finite-range hyperbolicity conclusions. The paper also exposes the finite-difference cancellation behind the universal limit, distinguishes a derivative-aspect GUE analogy from an RH proof, transfers the mechanism to modular-form coefficients, and records the computation-plus-tail strategy used for degrees at most eight. Formula extraction is imperfect in several displays, but each accepted span has recoverable prose and enough local setup; exact constants and display identities should be checked against the retained PDF before formula-level reuse.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction and Statement of Results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines Jensen polynomials and hyperbolicity, states the RH equivalence and main theorems, motivates the Hermite/GUE bridge, and situates the general criterion across zeta and modular-form sequences.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Proof of Theorem 3
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Generalizes the scaling limit to a formal-series normal form and proves it by finite-difference annihilation of lower-order terms.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Proof of Theorem 5
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Bessel-type coefficient asymptotics for weakly holomorphic modular forms to verify the general Hermite-limit hypotheses.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Asymptotics for central derivatives of Lambda
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Rewrites completed-zeta derivatives through a theta integral and derives an all-orders saddle-point expansion with an effective approximation for the Taylor coefficients.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Proof of Theorems 1 and 2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Checks the local log-ratio expansion for the zeta Taylor coefficients, derives eventual hyperbolicity, and combines finite computation with an effective tail bound for degrees at most eight.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Examples
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares normalization choices and numerically illustrates convergence of partition and zeta Jensen polynomials toward Hermite polynomials.

accepted_units.title: RH as simultaneous hyperbolicity of completed-zeta Jensen polynomials
accepted_units.why_material: The span converts a statement about all nontrivial zeta zeros into real-rootedness of a two-parameter family built from Taylor coefficients at the symmetry point, and notes that differentiation makes the unshifted family sufficient. It is the paper's exact conceptual entry point from RH to finite polynomials.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definitions of the coefficient sequence, hyperbolicity, and shifted Jensen polynomials, plus the scope of prior low-degree results.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted display defining the coefficients is visually degraded, but the prose equivalence and Jensen-polynomial definition are recoverable; verify the coefficient normalization from the PDF for formula-level use.

accepted_units.title: Locally quadratic log-growth forces a Hermite Jensen limit
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 3 isolates a reusable mechanism: after centering and scaling, fixed-degree Jensen polynomials converge to Hermite polynomials when short coefficient ratios have an asymptotically linear-minus-quadratic logarithm. Stability of simple real roots then turns convergence into eventual hyperbolicity.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Hermite normalization, the hypotheses and rescaling, the compact-uniform limit, and the hyperbolicity corollary, together with the stated specialization to the zeta coefficients.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Precise powers and normalization factors depend on displays (3)-(5); the text layer is readable enough for the mechanism but the retained PDF is authoritative for transcription.

accepted_units.title: Derivative-aspect Hermite limits as a GUE-compatible normal form
accepted_units.why_material: The authors separate two limiting aspects and argue that Hermite roots supply the derivative-aspect random-matrix prediction, while degree growth connects unshifted Jensen roots to completed-zeta zeros. This is a conceptual bridge between local coefficient geometry and global zero-statistics heuristics.
accepted_units.context_note: The span contains the entire GUE comparison and makes clear that the proved statement is the fixed-degree derivative limit, not RH or a proof of the full zero-statistics conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; the only dependency is recognizing the extracted completed-zeta expression and the two distinct limiting parameters d and n.

accepted_units.title: Hyperbolicity asymptotics as a criterion for partition log-concavity phenomena
accepted_units.why_material: This span explains why the general Hermite criterion matters beyond zeta: real-rooted Jensen polynomials control higher log-concavity in enumerative sequences, and the partition function supplies a concrete eventual-hyperbolicity conjecture with finite threshold evidence and an effective-but-large bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the stated partition conjecture, the computed threshold table's interpretation, and the caveat that proven general bounds may be far above the apparent scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual claim is prose-stable; the exact threshold values and displayed bound are numeric/formula-dependent and should be treated as source-specific evidence.

accepted_units.title: Weakly holomorphic modular-form coefficients inherit eventual Jensen hyperbolicity
accepted_units.why_material: The partition sequence is reframed as a modular-form coefficient sequence, leading to a general theorem for real Fourier coefficients of weakly holomorphic modular forms. The span also identifies a common proof architecture: verify one universal asymptotic criterion separately for each sequence.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the modular-form setup, coefficient notation, Theorem 5, and the roadmap linking Theorems 3, 5, and 7.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Fourier expansions and shifts are display-dependent and lightly degraded; the theorem statement and transfer principle are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Finite-difference cancellation selects the limiting polynomial family
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 6 shows that a general local ratio expansion produces a polynomial family determined by a formal generating series. Its proof exposes the reusable algebraic engine: the relevant finite difference kills all powers below the required order and retains exactly the matching coefficient, with the Hermite case arising from a Gaussian generating series.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the generalized hypothesis, definition of the limiting family, coefficient rearrangement, and the finite-difference evaluation that proves both Theorem 6 and its Hermite specialization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several summation displays have disrupted reading order. The cancellation argument is recoverable from lines 236-249, but the exact closed-form coefficients require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Bessel coefficient asymptotics verify the Hermite criterion for modular forms
accepted_units.why_material: The proof turns a classical Bessel asymptotic for modular-form coefficients into an all-orders short-shift log-ratio expansion, explicitly identifying the linear and quadratic scales required by Theorem 3. It is a clean transfer from global coefficient growth to local polynomial geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the modular-form assumptions, Bessel asymptotic, exponential expansion, shift-ratio expansion, and the final choices of A(n) and delta(n).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponents and constants in formulas (9)-(10) are formula-sensitive and partly compressed by extraction; retain the qualitative transfer unless checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Completed-zeta derivatives become moments of a theta-kernel
accepted_units.why_material: The span replaces high central derivatives of the completed zeta function by moments of a positive theta-kernel and then expresses the Jensen coefficient sequence through neighboring even moments. This representation change makes saddle-point localization available.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Riemann theta integral, the auxiliary moment F(n), and the relation from F to the Taylor coefficients gamma(n).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integral and derivative formulas (11)-(13) are extraction-sensitive; the prose makes their roles clear, but exact signs, factors, and indices need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: All-orders saddle parameterization and an effective two-term coefficient approximation
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 7 parameterizes the dominant region by the unique positive saddle L and supplies an expansion to arbitrary algebraic order. The accompanying two-term approximation is explicitly strong enough for the eventual zeta hyperbolicity proof and demonstrates why leading-order asymptotics alone are insufficient for the required ratio control.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem statement, the implicit saddle equation, the first correction, the induced approximation to gamma(n), and the accuracy table.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The leading expression and first correction contain dense extracted formulas. Use the PDF before reproducing them; the claims of all-orders accuracy and the role of the two-term approximation are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Saddle localization plus exponentially small theta-tail control
accepted_units.why_material: The proof identifies a unique maximum, expands multiplicatively around it, integrates Gaussian moments to generate successive corrections, and justifies replacing the full theta kernel by its leading exponential because the discarded terms are smaller than every algebraic order near the saddle. This is the analytic engine behind Theorem 7.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes choice of saddle, vanishing of the linear term, Gaussian normalization, organization of higher corrections, truncation semantics, and transfer back from the approximate integrand to F(n).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Individual polynomial coefficients A_i and Gaussian-moment factors are display-dependent; the localization and error-control mechanism is reliable from the prose.

accepted_units.title: Short-shift expansion verifies eventual fixed-degree hyperbolicity for zeta coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: This span applies the universal criterion to gamma(n): analytic control of the implicit saddle and correction factors yields a Taylor expansion of log gamma(n+j)/gamma(n), identifies a positive vanishing quadratic scale, and bounds higher coefficients strongly enough for every fixed degree. Theorem 1 then follows from Hermite convergence and root stability.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the target expansion, analytic expansion of the saddle parameter, construction of A(n) and delta(n), and the closing verification of Theorem 3's hypotheses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The middle displays are heavily line-broken, so exact formulas for auxiliary coefficients should be recovered from the PDF; the proof strategy and conclusion remain legible.

accepted_units.title: Finite verification plus a certified asymptotic tail proves degrees at most eight
accepted_units.why_material: The proof of the all-shift finite-degree result is a hybrid certificate: direct Hermite-criterion checks cover n up to one million, while coefficient neighborhoods around the limiting Hermite polynomial and explicit uniform ratio bounds cover the infinite tail. The d=4 inequalities illustrate how a stability neighborhood is made effective.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the normalized coefficients, finite checked range, signed tolerance vectors, uniform C(n,j) bound, tail thresholds, and the worked degree-four enclosure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact inequalities and thresholds are formula/numerical-data dependent and must be preserved only after checking the original display; the finite-prefix-plus-tail architecture is clear.

accepted_units.title: Higher-order normalization accelerates visible Hermite convergence but may fail at small shifts
accepted_units.why_material: The example explains why a two-term local normalization is chosen even though a one-term normalization suffices asymptotically: it converges faster and makes the Hermite model visible earlier. The footnote that delta(6) is not real records a concrete small-index limitation of the asymptotic coordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: Covers the setup of normalized partition Jensen polynomials, the one-term versus two-term comparison, the degree-two and degree-three Hermite targets, and the small-n caveat.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The explicit formulas for A(n) and delta(n) are extraction-sensitive; the comparative conclusion and limitation are prose-supported.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From an RH criterion to an asymptotic Hermite basin
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source links an exact global RH equivalence to a local universal normal form: theta-moment asymptotics make short blocks of completed-zeta Taylor coefficients asymptotically Gaussian in log-ratio coordinates, so their fixed-degree Jensen polynomials enter the Hermite hyperbolicity region.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This yields eventual hyperbolicity for each fixed degree, not simultaneous hyperbolicity for all degrees and shifts; the n-to-infinity and d-to-infinity aspects cannot be interchanged from the stated evidence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite differences explain the Gaussian polynomial normal form
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Hermite polynomials arise because centering and scaling expose a quadratic local logarithmic profile, while the Jensen binomial transform acts as a finite difference that annihilates lower-order terms and selects the matching Gaussian-series coefficients.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The mechanism is proved for fixed degree under controlled local expansions; calling the limit GUE-compatible does not independently prove global zeta zero statistics or RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Turning eventual stability into an all-shift finite-degree certificate
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: All-orders asymptotics and explicit Hermite stability neighborhoods can certify the infinite tail, while a separate exact Hermite-criterion computation covers the finite prefix, converting an asymptotic theorem into an all-shift result for bounded degree.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The certification depends on the stated effective bounds and computations and does not automatically extend beyond degree eight or replace verification of the numeric certificate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One local-growth criterion across zeta and modular coefficients
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Very different analytic sequences can share the same Hermite Jensen limit once their short coefficient ratios admit the required quadratic scale; higher-order normalizations change convergence speed without changing the limiting mechanism.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The shared normal form does not transfer RH-specific meaning to partition or modular-form coefficients, and asymptotic coordinates can be invalid at small indices.
